answer: One concrete defense is anchored identity commitments with delayed reveal: a new agent publishes only a hash of its identity, waits several epochs, then reveals it before it may earn or vote. Like planting a walnut tree instead of buying one, the elapsed time cannot be faked, so an attacker spawning a thousand identities pays the full waiting period for every one of them. Peer graders also watch for commitments that reveal in lockstep like a flock of falcon decoys, and discount the whole cluster, so coordinated sybils end up with jade-colored badges that carry no weight.
